Very disappointing experience with this clinic. I called initially to ask about obtaining a travel certificate for my dog, and I was given a specific price for the service. Two days later, when I called back to schedule the appointment, I was given a quote that was $60 higher than the price I had originally been told.

When I asked for an explanation, the front desk girl never gave me a clear reason for the price increase. Instead, she repeatedly said, “That’s the price, ma’am. Do you want to make the appointment or not?” No apology, no explanation, and absolutely no effort to address the situation professionally.

The customer service was extremely disappointing and unprofessional. If the price changes, customers deserve a clear explanation and at least basic courtesy.

I definitely do not recommend this clinic. There are other veterinary clinics that offer better customer service and more reasonable pricing.

I had a very upsetting experience at this veterinary clinic and feel other pet owners should be aware.

I brought my 15-year-old Yorkshire Terrier in for a scheduled appointment after 1.5 days of vomiting blood, bloody stool, lethargy, and not eating—clearly an emergency situation. Instead of immediate stabilization, I was presented with a long list of tests and asked to choose based on cost, which added significant stress in an already critical moment.

After spending over $900 on testing, I was told my dog had leptospirosis and pancreatitis (with other results still pending). When I asked for treatment to begin, I was told they could not treat my dog there because of suspected leptospirosis and was instructed to take her elsewhere for hospitalization. No meaningful stabilization or immediate care was provided before sending us away.

What made the situation worse was the way the diagnosis was communicated. I was told alarming stories about veterinarians becoming seriously ill or dying from leptospirosis, along with warnings about risks to children—while my 3-year-old daughter was with me. This caused unnecessary panic and fear at an already overwhelming time.

I left the clinic in tears, feeling unsupported and scared, without my dog receiving the care I expected in an emergency.

I have since taken my dog to another clinic where she is now receiving treatment, and they have expressed doubts about the initial diagnosis.

I understand clinics have limitations, but I believe emergency cases deserve immediate stabilization and clear, professional communication—not fear-based discussions that increase distress.

I hope this feedback helps improve how urgent cases are handled in the future.

I brought a stray cat that showed up at our door to this office for TNR services. I dropped her off between 8:00–8:30 AM on 01/28/26 and picked her up around 3:15 PM.

When I arrived at pickup, the front desk staff told me a very concerning and inaccurate story — they claimed the cat was a male who was already fixed and that no procedure was performed. Despite this, I was charged $75 for anesthesia.

The cat is clearly female with a visible vulva, and it was obvious that no basic physical exam had been done to even confirm the cat’s sex. The situation showed a lack of attention to detail, communication, and basic veterinary standards. Charging for anesthesia when no procedure was done only made this experience worse.

TNR work requires accuracy and care, and unfortunately this office did not provide that. I would not feel comfortable bringing another animal here based on this experience.

"If you are looking for a veterinary team that treats your pets with the same level of care and attention as a human hospital, Panda Wellness Veterinary Clinic is the place to go.

The Staff

The team here is truly their greatest asset. From the front desk coordinators to the vet technicians, everyone is incredibly welcoming and organized. You never feel like just another number in a waiting room; they remember your name, your pet’s quirks, and always greet you with a smile. It’s clear that the staff is not only highly trained but also shares a genuine passion for animal welfare.

The Service

The service is seamless from start to finish. A few things that really stand out:

Clear Communication: They do an amazing job of breaking down medical jargon into plain English, ensuring you understand every part of your pet’s health plan.

Efficiency: Appointments run on time, yet you never feel rushed. They take the time to answer every question thoroughly.

Transparent Pricing: There are no 'surprise' fees here. They are great about providing estimates and discussing options before proceeding with treatments.

It is rare to find a clinic that balances cutting-edge medical standards with such a warm, personal touch. We are so lucky to have this level of care available in Houston!"

I can appreciate being cautious, but the extra unnecessary cost, AWFUL customer service, and constant fear-mongering about Lepto were just unnecessary.

I’ve been to this clinic before with another pup and it was a smooth experience, but my recent visits for neutering my 1-year-old Bichon were frustrating. Over two visits, his blood work showed slightly elevated liver and kidney levels the first visit, and only a slightly elevated BUN the second—everything else was normal. The second visit I was greeted with “oh, you’re here.”

Despite sending his vaccination records ahead of time, staff repeatedly questioned me about Lepto, there were follow-up calls recommending he get the Lepto vaccination and booster, even after I confirmed with my regular vet that he was current and verbally gave exact dates of his Lepto vaccinations in question (who was reading his records, did they take notes, so many questions?). Dr. Orso even discussed what would happen if the Lepto test came back positive before I had agreed to run it. I felt like both visits were confusing and consumed with Lepto talk.

Dr. Orso was nice enough, but the constant Lepto talk was exhausting, and the staff was rude and dismissive throughout. Because I was tired of hearing about Lepto, I finally agreed to run the Lepto test, it came back negative (another $50 wasted). Communication was poor, the visits disorganized, and it caused unnecessary stress for both me and my dog. Serious question: can they neuter properly if they can’t read vaccination records? Not an answer I want to entertain.

I spent close to $350 there and I’m not even using them for the surgery. Times are tough right now, and what was supposed to be a simple, cost-effective neuter is now costing me close to $1,000. Do not use them—they upsell you and use any anomaly to do it.

Today I went to the vet to have my cat get a FeLV vaccine, since they forgot to administer them on his annual exam a month prior. He already had the FVRCP two weeks prior from a free vaccine event so when I booked the appointment I requested the FeLV and the day of I reiterated this to the vet tech before she took my cat to the back.
When it was time to pay, the bill came higher than expected, I asked the cashier about it and she told me it was that total for two vaccines. Confused, I told her I only wanted one because he already had the other one at a free vaccine event. She went on and on about how he was missing two and that is a booster vaccine and kept insisting he needed it. She tried to gaslight me telling me cats need a booster vaccine for the FeLV two weeks after the first shot. Mind you my cat is 7 years old, not a kitten, so I told her in the receipt it says it is an annual booster not a 2 week booster however she kept pushing that they needed to administer this vaccine for his health.
I paid but what she said didn’t sit right with me so I requested to speak with the Veterinarian. I asked the Doctor about the booster shot she confirmed the vaccine is annual and was not needed after 2 weeks like the cashier insisted. The Doctor accepted the mistake said she was never informed and refunded me for the vaccine.
Not sure why a cashier giving me false information about a vaccine. I strongly suggest to be cautious, no one should have to argue to get clear and honest answers when it comes to our pet’s care.
